title: Fork's own flake templates and install docs pin the archived, unpatched upstream (fort-nix) instead of this fork
evidence: inputs.nix-bitcoin.url = "github:fort-nix/nix-bitcoin/release";  (also examples/container/flake.nix:13, examples/README.md:10 `nix run github:fort-nix/nix-bitcoin/release`, examples/README.md:21 and docs/install.md:213 `git clone https://github.com/fort-nix/nix-bitcoin`) — while helper/fetch-release refuses the same repo: "This repository is a maintained FORK; upstream's release artifacts do NOT contain this fork's fixes, so fetching them here would silently ship un-fixed code" and prescribes `github:ostermayer/nix-bitcoin/release`
attack_scenario: New user finds this fork (the maintained one), copies its primary template examples/flakes/flake.nix or follows docs/install.md step 1. They silently deploy archived upstream master: clightning-rest bound to 0.0.0.0 with RPCCOMMANDS=["*"] (full wallet withdraw API on all interfaces if enabled), lndconnect rebinding lnd's admin REST to 0.0.0.0 without onion, the DoS-able public RPC whitelist (scantxoutset/getblocktemplate), nbxplorer 2.6.7 (BTCPay security advisory), the onion-addresses root symlink-follow, and the clboss 0.16.1 fund-theft version in the stale nixpkgs pin. A network attacker then exercises those known bugs, e.g. `withdraw` via an exposed clightning-rest, ending in fund theft. No attacker action on this repo is needed; the fork's own docs deliver the victim to the vulnerable code.
impact: funds (known upstream fund-theft/admin-exposure bugs re-shipped to this fork's users), dos, secrets
false_positive_risk: Only if the fort-nix references are deliberate (e.g. maintainers intend templates to point upstream until their own release branch is trusted). But helper/fetch-release explicitly calls fetching upstream a silent-ship of un-fixed code, so the templates contradict the fork's stated stance. No runtime exploit in this repo itself; impact is realized only when a user onboards via these files.
recommendation: Point all user-facing refs at the fork: `github:ostermayer/nix-bitcoin/release` in examples/flakes/flake.nix, examples/container/flake.nix, examples/README.md, and the clone URL in docs/install.md. Grep `fort-nix` in CI to keep it from regressing.

title: btcpayserver joins nbxplorer's group, granting write access to nbxplorer's whole data dir (only needs to read one cookie file)
evidence: users.users.${cfg.btcpayserver.user} = { ... extraGroups = [ cfg.nbxplorer.group ]; ... } combined with systemd.tmpfiles.rules: "d '${cfg.nbxplorer.dataDir}' 0770 ${cfg.nbxplorer.user} ${cfg.nbxplorer.group} - -" (group rwx) and btcexplorercookiefile=${cfg.nbxplorer.dataDir}/.../.cookie
attack_scenario: Attacker exploits btcpayserver (internet-facing web app; the 2.4.2 unauthenticated-macaroon-theft advisory shows this class is real) and runs code as the btcpayserver user. Via group nbxplorer they can unlink/replace files in /var/lib/nbxplorer despite file-level 0600 perms: delete the Main/.cookie and DB (availability), or replace settings.config so the next nbxplorer start uses attacker-chosen bind/btcrpcurl (integrity/DoS). They cannot escalate further: nbxplorer holds no keys, the bitcoind RPC password for the btcpayserver user was already readable to them via the same group, and postgres peer-auth as the nbxplorer OS user is not obtainable. Payoff is limited to destroying/corrupting the watch-only indexer that btcpayserver depends on.
false_positive_risk: Inherited unchanged from upstream nix-bitcoin, and the cookie must be group-readable by design; only the directory-wide rwx is the over-grant. Exploit requires a btcpayserver RCE first, at which point the marginal gain is small.
recommendation: Have nbxplorer stage the cookie (or a copy) into a btcpayserver-readable 0440 file at a dedicated path (same pattern as /run/lnd macaroons) and drop btcpayserver from group nbxplorer; or set the data dir 0750 and ACL-read the cookie only.

title: nodeinfo checks a misspelled unit name 'onion-adresses', making its failure guard dead code
attack_scenario: None with security payoff: when onion-addresses.service is enabled but failed, nodeinfo prints per-service read errors instead of the intended clear fatal message. Operator-UX defect only; is_enabled on the misspelled name always returns false so the guard never fires.
impact: none (cosmetic; fails open to a slightly worse error message)
false_positive_risk: None; the typo is unambiguous. Reported as info per the brief's evidence discipline.
recommendation: Fix the spelling to 'onion-addresses' in all three occurrences.
